deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated layers: mathematical jottings in ink at the top left, and a draft Italian letter in pencil below.

(1) Period scheme. The first lines are a period table in Riemann's usual layout: an integral name, then its periods across the canonical cycles.
- v_1 has periods (πi, 0 | b_{1,1}, …) and v_2 has (0, πi | b_{1,2}, …). These are normalised integrals: πi·δ on the A-cycles and the symmetric b on the B-cycles.
- A second copy v'_1 has periods (πi, 0 | b_{1,1}, b_{2,1}).
- A third integral u_1 has period πi.
- This continues the previous page. There Riemann wrote the general period lattice u_ν + n_ν πi + Σ m_μ a_{ν,μ}, a product ∏_{ν=1}^{λ²} ϑ(v + a^{(ν)}) over λ² translates, and division of periods by λ (v/λ, πi/λ). That is the setting of order-λ theta transformation, i.e. λ-sheeted unramified covers.
- My reading: u, v, v' are the three copies (lifts to the three sheets) of a base integral on an unramified 3-sheeted cyclic cover.

(2) Eigen-decomposition. Let ρ = e^{2πi/3}. Riemann forms
- w^{(0)}_ν = (u_ν + v_ν + v'_ν)/3,
- w^{(1)}_ν = (u_ν + ρ v_ν + ρ² v'_ν)/3,
- w^{(2)}_ν = (u_ν + ρ² v_ν + ρ v'_ν)/3.

This is the discrete Fourier transform over Z/3. The following implicit steps are mine:
- Inversion: w^{(0)} + w^{(1)} + w^{(2)} = u, because 1 + ρ + ρ² = 0. Likewise v = Σ ρ^{-k} w^{(k)} and v' = Σ ρ^{-2k} w^{(k)}.
- Equivariance: if the deck transformation σ permutes u → v → v' → u, then σ w^{(k)} = ρ^{-k} w^{(k)}.
- Consequence: w^{(0)} is invariant and descends to the base surface. w^{(1)} and w^{(2)} are the ρ- and ρ²-eigencomponents. These are integrals with multiplicative periods (factors ρ^{±1}), i.e. Prym-type integrals; on the Jacobian side they span the Prym part.

(3) Counting. Riemann writes Σ_1^{6n−6} and, separately, 2n−2.
- On a base surface of genus n an abelian differential has 2n−2 zeros.
- Its pullback to the unramified 3-sheeted cover has 3(2n−2) = 6n−6 zeros.
- So the cover has genus n' with 2n'−2 = 6n−6, i.e. n' = 3n−2 (Riemann–Hurwitz, unramified case).
- The next page treats the general λ-sheeted case. Its indices p−1, p and 1/λ, 1/2 fit genus λ(p−1)+1: there Riemann computes the quadratic form (the period matrix) of the cover in terms of r, b.

Purpose: to transform/decompose theta functions of the cover via the cyclic group action, a precursor of the Schottky–Jung/Prym decomposition.

(4) Letter (pencil), addressed to 'Sig. Giuseppe Franchi a Latignano presso Cascina nel Piano di Pisa', marked 'franco' (postage paid). Text: 'Our daughter now takes my wife's breast. It only remains, then, that you look for a wet-nurse for your own baby and come as soon as possible to our house to fetch your child. We live outside Porta alle Piagge, opposite the church of S. Michele, in the villa of Lieutenant General Fraser.'
- Riemann's daughter Ida was born in Pisa in December 1863, which dates the draft to about the beginning of 1864.
- The church is plausibly S. Michele degli Scalzi, near the Piagge.
- The Franchi family's wife seems to have been the wet-nurse.
- The small pencil sketch looks like a chair or frame and is not mathematical.
errors: No mathematical errors visible; the jottings are skeletal.
The precise roles of u, v, v' (lifts on three sheets vs. three different integrals) are not stated and are inferred.
The B-periods of v'_1 are written b_{1,1}, b_{2,1} while those of v_1 are b_{1,1}, b_{1,2}. This is harmless by the symmetry b_{μν} = b_{νμ}, but the table is incomplete.

results.what: Decomposition of the integrals of a 3-sheeted cyclic unramified cover into ρ-eigencomponents (u + ρ^k v + ρ^{2k} v')/3
results.modern_name: Isotypic/eigenspace decomposition of the Jacobian under the deck group; Prym (multiplicative-period) differentials; Prym variety of a cyclic cover
results.usually_credited_to: Prym (Prym differentials, 1860s–1880s); Wirtinger (1895) and Schottky–Jung (1909) for the Prym-variety viewpoint

results.what: Zero count 6n−6 = 3(2n−2) for a 3-sheeted unramified cover, giving genus 3n−2
Normalised period scheme (πi on A-cycles, symmetric b on B-cycles)

deep.surprise_reason: Explicit use of cube-root-of-unity eigencombinations of integrals on an unramified cyclic 3-sheeted cover, in the context of theta transformation of order λ, anticipates the Prym/Schottky–Jung decomposition. This is consistent with Riemann's known influence on Prym, but such a concrete unpublished trace is a notable detail. The page itself is only a sketch, without results.

'Sig.' precedes 'Lieutenant General Fraser'; the inserted phrase 'nella villa del' belongs before 'Sig.'.
'franco[?]' is correct: the postal mark 'franco' (postage paid).
The '$\alpha$[?]' under the first table is a small mark (tilde/ditto sign), probably not α.
The fourth row is likely 'u_1 πi' (the symbol looks blotted or overwritten), consistent with u, v, v' below.
The top-right entries read b_{1,1}, b_{1,2} (the first possibly b_{1,1} with an overwritten subscript).
